key_concept: Morphine is an opioid alkaloid obtained from the latex of the poppy plant (Papaver somniferum), and it is medically used as a very effective sedative and painkiller, especially for patients after surgery.
steps: The question asks for a drug that does two things: it acts as a sedative (calms or induces sleep) and as an analgesic (relieves pain).
Morphine is an opioid. It binds to specific opioid receptors in the central nervous system and the gastrointestinal tract, which depresses pain perception and produces sedation.
It is extracted from the latex of the poppy plant, Papaver somniferum. It is a legally prescribed medicine for post-surgical pain, although it is abused as a narcotic.
Interferons are glycoproteins secreted by virus-infected cells that protect neighbouring cells from viral infection. They have no sedative or painkilling role.
Antibiotics kill or inhibit bacteria, and anti-retroviral drugs suppress HIV replication. Neither relieves pain nor sedates.
Only morphine fits both parts of the description, so option (3) is correct and matches the NTA key.
why_not_others: Antibiotics are tempting because they are routinely given after surgery, but they only prevent bacterial infection and do not relieve pain. Interferons and anti-retroviral drugs are antiviral agents with no analgesic or sedative action.
common_trap: Students pick antibiotics because they associate post-surgery care with them, even though antibiotics only prevent infection and are not painkillers.
time_saving_tip: Remember the textbook line from the drugs section: 'Morphine is a very effective sedative and painkiller, useful in patients who have undergone surgery.' Seeing 'sedative and painkiller' should point you straight to morphine.
